claim_scope: Role-based AI review of three exact-CAD renders; no human preference study and no physical object

findings.finding: The bishop, queen, and king share a tall tapered cone-and-collar body. Their crown cues are too small relative to the common body, so the three ranks collapse toward one silhouette at ordinary board scale.

Stone and Steel differ clearly in render color, but their geometric difference is concentrated around base grooves and the lower pedestal. The upper bodies retain nearly the same tapered language, so neutral-material and low-color-vision side identity is not established.

The exact top view distinguishes rooks and knights, but the circular minor/royal pieces depend on small central marks. No scored neutral-material classification run exists, so the required rank and side thresholds are not met.

The water-tower pawns, stepped rooks, bridge-like knights, and restrained board read as architectural rather than gift-shop landmarks. The conical bishop/queen/king family is less specifically Manhattan and needs more distinct Art Deco or neo-Gothic massing.

panel_execution: One AI evaluation applied six explicit player and critic lenses; the roles are not represented as independent humans.
